analysis.title: Midterm Election Results: Decisive for Democrats
key_insights: Democrats have won control of the House and Senate, although some races are still being counted. The results point toward MS's 'cohesive' Democratic majority scenario.

The most important result for data center development was the Texas gubernatorial election, where Democrat Gina Hinojosa won. Her platform included a moratorium on new data center approvals, and MS sees risk of many projects being delayed significantly.

In Ohio, Democrat Dr. Amy Acton's win creates significant risk of data center delays. The largest project at risk is a 10 gigawatt project involving NVIDIA and a major US AI lab. Amazon's 1.5 gigawatt Fayette County facility is under construction.
MS expects an incremental, idiosyncratic headwind to AI sentiment, leaving the broader AI capex narrative intact. It expects a split between states that permit new data centers and those that do not.

Index-level uncertainty from the change in control can be a headwind to US equities, similar to 2022 midterm volatility. Since 1982, large-cap equities gained about 15% cap-weighted and 16% equal-weighted in the six months after midterms, and about 22% over the following year.

MS says the midterms are the most obvious clearing event and could mark the final phase of the rolling correction discussed since the summer. Renewed military escalation with Iran or additional tariffs are near-term risks.

MS keeps its overweight on global equities and underweight on core fixed income. The midterm results do not materially change oil prices, ex-US fiscal risks or the AI capex cycle that drive that allocation.

The party-line reconciliation route is closed from January, which removes the main upside risk to Treasury borrowing needs. Pre-election prediction markets gave single-digit odds to unified Republican control, so little of that supply was priced.

Delayed SNAP and Medicaid cuts could add 2-7 year issuance. MS sees only modest belly underperformance. Bills maturing around the debt-limit x-date could cheapen, and late-3Q27 SOFR/FF basis longs could become more attractive.
MS rates strategists estimate the debt limit becomes binding by March 2027 and the x-date falls in late 3Q27. The more likely course is that the debt ceiling stays a late-2027 catalyst.

In FX, MS expects trading consistent with its defense regime, favoring JPY, CHF and EUR against USD. AUD may lag on crosses on AI sentiment, CAD may underperform low yielders on tariff risk, and NOK/SEK may fall on less geopolitical escalation risk.
A delay to SNAP and Medicaid cuts could add up to 0.4pp to 2027 personal consumption. MS sees deficits staying near 6% of GDP even with the cuts extended.

AI financing focus could shift toward chip financing from power-shell financing, since construction and energization, the stages most exposed to policy, are usually complete by the chip-installation stage. This could contribute to a more sustained flattening of credit curves.

Healthcare: a Democratic sweep is seen as positive for Medicaid-focused managed care (CNC, MOH), with a more muted reaction for UNH and CVS. Medicare Advantage names such as HUM could dip on a knee-jerk basis.

Lame-duck calendar: the CR runs through December 11. The FY27 NDAA is expected to pass by year-end, possibly with export control provisions (MATCH Act, AI OVERWATCH, Chip Security, RASA). MS views a GOP 'Reconciliation 3.0' as an uphill battle. Trump and Xi may meet at APEC (Nov 18-19) and the G20 (Dec 14-15).

Texas power: ERCOT interconnection requests reached about 474 GW, more than 5x record peak demand, with data centers about 90% of new requests. Texas paused parts of its interconnection process in August after an audit order.

MS expects knee-jerk underperformance in IPPs, led by VST, then NRG and CEG. TLN and PEG have no Texas exposure and should outperform relatively. MS values VST's current assets at about $180 per share against $140, CEG at $249 against $263, NRG at $129 against $96, and TLN at $430 against $357.

MS expects underperformance in power equipment (GEV, INIO, BE) from slower data center growth, mainly multiple compression. GEV has the most diversified exposure. INIO is the most sensitive, with possible slower bookings in 2029+.

Texas-exposed utilities: CNP is seen as most sensitive, trading at about an 11% premium. SRE, AEP, XEL and ETR also face likely modest downward revisions and multiple compression. MS expects investors to rotate into AEE, ED and DUK.

Among Texas-exposed data center developers, MS is watching GLXY's Helios II, CIFR's Colchis and MARA's project for possible freezes. It sees projects under construction (GLXY Helios I Phases II and III, HUT Beacon Point, CIFR projects) as less exposed. WULF and APLD are seen as relative beneficiaries.
MS has high conviction that WMB is materially mispriced relative to behind-the-meter data center power growth likely to become visible over the next 12-24 months.

risk_factors: Further Texas and Ohio data center restrictions, including moratoria, permit freezes and regulator appointments, could delay projects.
Renewed military escalation with Iran or additional tariffs after the elections.
Executive-led policy on tariffs, geopolitics, trade, deregulation and export controls keeps policy uncertainty elevated.
A Republican-led reconciliation bill remains an uphill but possible upside risk to Treasury borrowing needs in the lame duck.
Debt limit fight in 2027, with the x-date in late 3Q27.
Elevated AI-related corporate credit issuance could widen spreads, especially in lower-quality credit.
A shutdown after the December 11 CR expiry would delay data releases.
Legislation targeting AI buildout, such as reversing OBBBA immediate expensing or a tax on compute, is seen as unlikely given presidential opposition.
vol_and_positioning: MS says investors broadly anticipated a Democratic sweep with a narrow Senate majority. The Texas gubernatorial win on top of that could add near-term volatility.
CNP is well-owned and trades at about an 11% premium, so it could be most exposed to a downside correction.
Narrower legislative variance means lower rate volatility under a Republican hold.
Late-3Q27 SOFR/FF basis longs could become more attractive if debt limit negotiations drag on.
Bills maturing around the x-date could cheapen unless the lame-duck session raises the debt limit.
geopolitical: Renewed military escalation with Iran is a near-term risk after the elections.
Trump and Xi may meet at APEC in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19 and at the G20 in Miami on Dec 14-15. MS's base case is managed competition with limited agreements.
Congress is expected to drive more export controls through the FY27 NDAA (MATCH Act, AI OVERWATCH, Chip Security, RASA) while the administration prioritizes stability with China.
The USMCA review and targeted tariffs remain executive-led risks.
Stronger congressional resistance to renewed geopolitical escalation could pressure NOK/SEK.

tension_points.theme: AI capex versus data center restrictions
tension_points.bull_case: Restrictions are idiosyncratic and state-specific, and MS's base case is that top-down US tech investment stays intact. This supports global equity earnings and the overweight on equities.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic wins in Texas and Ohio could bring moratoria, permit freezes and regulator changes, delaying many projects and hurting AI sentiment and Texas-exposed power and data center names.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Hinojosa executive order pausing new Texas data center projects, or freezes on the final classification of Batch-process projects, would challenge the view that the effect stays limited.

tension_points.bull_case: Since 1982, large-cap equities gained about 15% cap-weighted over six months after midterms, and the results could mark the final phase of the rolling correction.
tension_points.bear_case: Uncertainty from the change in control, similar to 2022, plus the Texas gubernatorial win could cause near-term volatility. Iran escalation or new tariffs add risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed military escalation with Iran or additional tariffs following the elections.

tension_points.bull_case: Closing the reconciliation route removes the main upside risk to borrowing needs, with only modest belly underperformance from delayed SNAP and Medicaid cuts.
tension_points.bear_case: Democrats could attach priorities to a debt limit increase, drawing out a resolution and cheapening bills around the x-date.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A lame-duck debt limit increase would remove the x-date premium in bills and keep Treasury on track to raise coupon auction sizes in February 2027.
